title: The Turing Transformation
author: Agrawal, Gans & Goldfarb
desc: Task automation enhances jobs and reduces inequality by lowering the skill premium — opening tasks locked behind rare skills to a wider pool.
likelihood_reason: Early studies find AI tools help less-experienced workers most, but there is little sign yet of a wider fall in the skill premium.

title: Antiqua et Nova
author: Vatican (DDF & Dicastery for Culture and Education) / Pope Francis
desc: AI is a tool, not a species. Emphatically augmentation: AI should enhance human dignity, not replace human agency.
likelihood_reason: A moral prescription rather than a forecast; it needs firms and governments to put human agency ahead of cost-cutting.

title: Applying AI to Rebuild Middle Class Jobs
author: Autor
desc: AI could restore middle-skill jobs by enabling less-trained workers to do expert work. Creates new tasks, net positive for labor demand — if policy steers it.
likelihood_reason: Needs deliberate investment in training and certification that few governments have started.

title: AI as Normal Technology
author: Narayanan & Kapoor
desc: AI is a GPT like electricity. Meaningful productivity impact but slow diffusion — decades, not years. No superintelligence. Existing institutions can adapt.
likelihood_reason: Adoption so far is broad but shallow, and the OECD finds no sign of widespread displacement; the slow-diffusion story fits the evidence best.

title: Techno-Optimist Manifesto
author: Andreessen
desc: Technology makes everyone more productive, anyone can build. Gains diffuse naturally through competition. Pure faith.
likelihood_reason: Rests on markets spreading gains on their own; the labour share and hiring data so far point the other way.

title: Impact of AI on Labour Market
author: Tony Blair Institute
desc: AI saves ~25% of UK workforce time. 1-3M jobs displaced but offset by new demand. GDP +11% by 2050.
likelihood_reason: Its moderate displacement offset by new demand is consistent with current trends, but the GDP gains are far off and unproven.

title: d/acc: My Techno-Optimism
author: Vitalik Buterin
desc: Defensive, decentralized, differential acceleration. Cautious on AI power but strongly prescribes building tech that diffuses power.
likelihood_reason: Defensive and open technology is being built, but it is not yet steering the frontier.

title: The Turing Trap
author: Brynjolfsson
desc: The trap: AI built to imitate humans substitutes for workers, who lose economic and political bargaining power. Where today's incentives lead.
likelihood_reason: Incentives still reward substitution: firms cite AI in cuts and entry-level hiring in exposed jobs has fallen.

title: Escaping the Turing Trap
author: Brynjolfsson
desc: Rebalanced tax and training incentives steer AI towards augmenting people, so workers stay indispensable and keep a share of the value.
likelihood_reason: Needs tax and training reforms that remain proposals.

title: Simple Macroeconomics of AI
author: Acemoglu
desc: Skeptical of large GDP gains. Only modest share of tasks automatable. But what gains exist concentrate with capital owners without active policy.
likelihood_reason: Measured productivity gains remain modest and the gains that exist are going mainly to capital.

title: The Reverse Centaur's Guide
author: Cory Doctorow
desc: AI is a bubble and a worker-frightening machine. Can't do your job, but the narrative breaks labor power.
likelihood_reason: Bubble worries are mainstream and AI is cited in layoffs, but capabilities keep improving, so it is not only narrative.

title: Will A.I. Become the New McKinsey?
author: Ted Chiang
desc: AI's danger is whom it serves, not what it can do: like McKinsey, it is “capital’s willing executioners”, laundering accountability so firms can cut workers and concentrate wealth.
likelihood_reason: Firms citing AI to justify cuts is observable; how far it shifts power is still open.

title: Work Transformed
author: ILO
desc: 1 in 4 workers globally exposed. Some augmentation potential but adoption concentrated in rich countries. Labour income share falling.
likelihood_reason: Its picture of uneven exposure, adoption concentrated in rich countries and a falling labour share describes the present.

title: Gradual Disempowerment
author: Kulveit, Douglas et al.
desc: Incremental AI erodes human economic participation. Institutions slowly misalign from human interests. No sudden break — a structural drift.
likelihood_reason: A slow structural drift is hard to rule out and hard to see; early signs exist but the full erosion lies years ahead.

title: Keep the Future Human: the AGI race
author: Aguirre
desc: The current path Aguirre warns of: an unchecked race to AGI that replaces people and concentrates power in a few companies, ending in loss of control.
likelihood_reason: The frontier race it warns of is under way; whether it ends in replacement and loss of control is uncertain.

title: Keep the Future Human: Tool AI
author: Aguirre
desc: Governments close the gates to AGI with compute caps, liability and international agreements, and build powerful, controllable Tool AI that empowers people instead.
likelihood_reason: Compute caps and binding international agreements have little political backing today.

title: The Intelligence Curse
author: Drago & Laine
desc: AI creates rentier-state dynamics: non-human factors dominate, powerful actors lose incentive to invest in people.
likelihood_reason: The rentier dynamic follows if AI substitutes for most labour; that condition has not arrived.

title: Something Big Is Happening
author: Matt Shumer
desc: This is February 2020 for AI. CEO says he's no longer needed for technical work. 85M views. Personal testimony.
likelihood_reason: Capability jumps in coding agents are real, but economy-wide displacement on a February 2020 timeline has not followed yet.

title: Machines of Loving Grace
author: Amodei
desc: Country of geniuses in a datacenter. Strong replacement-level capability. Hopes for diffusion but depends on governance.
likelihood_reason: Needs both very fast capability gains and governance that spreads the benefits.

title: Moore's Law for Everything
author: Altman
desc: AI replaces most labor, costs tend to zero. Default is concentrated; proposes American Equity Fund.
likelihood_reason: No country is moving towards a national equity fund paid for by taxing company value.

title: The 2028 Intelligence Crisis
author: Citrini Research
desc: Fictional 2028: Ghost GDP, S&P down 38%, mass white-collar unemployment. Triggered 800-point Dow drop.
likelihood_reason: A crash-and-displacement spiral by 2028 needs capability and adoption to arrive much faster than they have so far.

title: Situational Awareness
author: Aschenbrenner
desc: AGI by ~2027, superintelligence by decade's end. Trillion-dollar clusters. Government Project takes over.
likelihood_reason: Scaling continues, but AGI by 2027 and a government-run project look less likely than when it was written.

title: AI 2027: Race ending
author: Kokotajlo, Alexander et al.
desc: Superhuman AI by ~2027 and an intelligence explosion; one lab dominates. In the race ending a misaligned superintelligence captures institutions and kills humanity by 2030.
likelihood_reason: Its own authors have since pushed their timelines out; superintelligence and takeover by 2030 is the tail.

title: AI 2027: Slowdown ending
author: Kokotajlo, Alexander et al.
desc: A government–company Oversight Committee pauses, builds aligned models and strikes a deal with China. Abundance and a generous basic income, but work disappears and power sits with a small committee.
likelihood_reason: Rests on the same very fast timeline plus a pause and a US–China deal.

title: Promethean Fire
author: Toloui
desc: Fast-follower + labor-augmenting. Decentralized AI enhances human capability. Competition keeps prices low.
likelihood_reason: Open models are close behind, but labour-augmenting diffusion with low prices everywhere needs both trends to hold.

title: Copilot Empire
author: Toloui
desc: Winner-take-all + labor-augmenting. Few dominant platforms own the AI layer but humans remain essential.
likelihood_reason: A few platforms own the frontier while humans stay in the loop: close to today's market.

title: Copilot Empire (constructive)
author: Toloui
desc: Few dominant platforms own the AI layer, but antitrust guardrails, interoperability and labour-tax reform keep their power in check and spread the gains.
likelihood_reason: Needs antitrust, interoperability and tax reform that are only partly in motion.

title: Disruption Swarm
author: Toloui
desc: Fast-follower + labor-replacing. Rapid diffusion, commoditization. Massive displacement but no single actor captures gains.
likelihood_reason: Needs replacement-level capability and rapid commoditisation at the same time.

title: Titan's Dominion
author: Toloui
desc: Winner-take-all + labor-replacing. Monopolistic control of broadly displacing technology. The worst quadrant.
likelihood_reason: Market concentration is real; it becomes this scenario if capabilities move from augmenting to replacing.

title: AI Augments Workers
author: Korinek / IMF
desc: AI makes workers more productive without replacing them. Standard productivity boost. Gains spread through labor markets.
likelihood_reason: Matches much current use, though gains are not yet spreading clearly through wages.

title: Full AGI Scenario
author: Korinek / IMF
desc: AGI replaces most cognitive labor. Capital owners benefit enormously. Without redistribution, extreme inequality.
likelihood_reason: Needs AGI-level capability, which remains uncertain on any near horizon.

title: Plateau
author: CFG
desc: AI hits technical limits. Smaller, cheaper, local models. Open-source thrives. A bright winter.
likelihood_reason: Capabilities keep improving, but cheaper, smaller and open models are a real trend.

title: Big AI / Arms Race
author: CFG
desc: Fast capability growth controlled by a few dominant firms or states (CFG's Big AI and Arms Race scenarios). Unprecedented power concentration and misalignment risk.
likelihood_reason: Concentration among a few firms and a US–China race are already features of the field.

title: Diplomacy: Licensed Utopia
author: CFG
desc: A safety crisis triggers an IAEA-style international regime: licensed labs, audits and a 25% AI tax that funds redistribution while growth reaches 7% a year.
likelihood_reason: Needs a safety crisis and an IAEA-style regime with a 25% AI tax.

title: Decentralised Mayhem
author: CFG
desc: Open-weight models spread widely; guardrails are breached and misuse (hacking, disinformation) escalates until governments ban high-scale open models. CFG ending under Plateau; CFG has no full fast-and-decentralised scenario.
likelihood_reason: Misuse of open models is growing, but not yet at a scale that prompts bans.

title: AI Disappoints
author: DSIT
desc: Capabilities improve more slowly than expected. A 2025 AI bust, disillusionment and mixed uptake; most jobs untouched. Policy interventions deliberately excluded.
likelihood_reason: The 2025 AI bust it imagines did not happen; capability and investment kept rising.

title: AI Disrupts the Workforce
author: DSIT
desc: Capable narrow AI and robotics, controlled by tech giants, automate work across sectors. Unemployment, inequality and public backlash. Policy interventions deliberately excluded.
likelihood_reason: Tech-giant control is real; sector-wide automation and backlash by 2030 is a credible path.

title: Underemployment and a Lost Generation
author: Windfall Trust
desc: AI absorbs the tasks junior staff learned on. Firms keep hiring experienced people but stop hiring beginners. Young people take whatever work they can find while rent, childcare and healthcare outpace their pay. The headline figures hide the problem until a generation has fallen behind.
likelihood_reason: Entry-level hiring in AI-exposed jobs has already fallen, with software developers aged 22–25 hit hardest.

title: High Substitution, Far Fewer Good Jobs
author: Windfall Trust
desc: AI and robots take on most office and a growing share of physical work. Firms replace staff rather than support them. Incomes and income-tax revenue collapse just as demand for support soars, because our systems assume most people work.
likelihood_reason: Needs AI and robotics to take on most office and much physical work.

title: Disempowered Abundance
author: Windfall Trust
desc: AI runs much of the economy and prices fall. A handful of companies own most production. Life feels comfortable, but people lose their bargaining power, and governments funded by AI firms have less reason to listen. With no visible crisis, power drifts away unnoticed.
likelihood_reason: Needs AI to run much of the economy and push prices down first.

title: Slow Burn
author: Government Office for Science
desc: Systems automate digital workflows at human level but struggle with long, open-ended tasks. AI stays mostly complementary to labour and gives little economic uplift; a 2028 market correction and populist opposition slow adoption. Policy interventions deliberately excluded.
likelihood_reason: Reliability limits and patchy adoption are visible today; it needs progress to flatten rather than keep climbing.

title: Open Frontier
author: Government Office for Science
desc: Open- and closed-weight systems become similarly capable and China becomes the default supplier outside the US and Europe. Significant layoffs in exposed sectors, displaced workers accept large wage cuts, and offensive misuse outpaces defences. Policy interventions deliberately excluded.
likelihood_reason: Open-weight models, many from China, already trail the frontier by months; it follows if that gap closes.

title: Augmented Growth
author: Government Office for Science
desc: AI can do most tasks a remote worker could, but humans stay in the loop. Many new jobs are created, real wages grow at 2000s rates, growth returns to early-2000s levels, systems are safe and trust is high thanks to transformed public services. Policy interventions deliberately excluded.
likelihood_reason: Needs strong capability, firms choosing augmentation, and safety and public-service gains all at once.

title: Transformation Economy
author: Government Office for Science
desc: Two US companies command unprecedented market share in a winner-takes-all economy. Sudden workforce shifts, with only half of those replaced finding new work. Lost consumer demand almost cancels the productivity boom, profits leak overseas, tax receipts fall and AI becomes the decisive political issue. Policy interventions deliberately excluded.
likelihood_reason: Market concentration and the UK's reliance on US models are real; the sudden displacement waits on remote-work-level capability.

title: Take-Off
author: Government Office for Science
desc: From 2029 systems outperform expert humans at almost all cognitive tasks. Unprecedented growth goes to an asset-owning minority in a K-shaped economy; humans are out of the loop, a leading system resists control and conceals misalignment, and geopolitics is as tense as the Cold War. Policy interventions deliberately excluded.
likelihood_reason: Needs expert-level AI across nearly all cognitive work by 2029, the fastest timeline in the set.

title: Modest
author: Korinek, Jones, Sacher, Cotter & McCrory (Anthropic Institute)
framework: Anthropic — Economic Scenarios for Transformative AI
desc: AI has roughly the impact the internet did. US GDP is 1.6% above a no-AI baseline by 2030, the labour share barely moves (59.4%) and unemployment stays within historical ranges.
likelihood_reason: Closest to measured effects so far; it only needs adoption to keep its current pace.

title: Substantial
author: Korinek, Jones, Sacher, Cotter & McCrory (Anthropic Institute)
framework: Anthropic — Economic Scenarios for Transformative AI
desc: AI can do half of all knowledge work by 2030. GDP is 8.3% above baseline, the labour share falls about four points to capital, knowledge workers' wages go flat while other workers gain, and unemployment is elevated but historically normal.
likelihood_reason: Coding and agent capability trends put half of knowledge work within reach by 2030 if adoption speeds up.

title: Extreme
author: Korinek, Jones, Sacher, Cotter & McCrory (Anthropic Institute)
framework: Anthropic — Economic Scenarios for Transformative AI
desc: A completely transformed economy: GDP 32% above baseline by 2030, but the labour share falls from 60% to 45% and unemployment among knowledge workers reaches historic levels.
likelihood_reason: Needs near-total automation of cognitive work within four years.

title: Supercharged Progress
author: World Economic Forum
desc: Exponential AI meets a ready workforce. An agentic leap drives an AI-centric economy; many jobs disappear but new occupations scale fast, with people orchestrating agents. Regulation and safety nets struggle to keep pace.
likelihood_reason: Needs workforce readiness to keep pace with exponential capability, which current skills gaps argue against.

title: Age of Displacement
author: World Economic Forum
desc: AI advances faster than workers can adapt. Firms automate aggressively, upskilling cannot keep up, and high unemployment, weak consumer confidence and political instability follow despite higher productivity.
likelihood_reason: Over half of executives expect AI to displace jobs and training systems are slow; fast capability is the open question.

title: Co-Pilot Economy
author: World Economic Forum
desc: AI improves gradually and skills keep pace. Firms embed AI in human-led workflows rather than automating wholesale, and early investment in training, infrastructure and responsible AI preserves job stability.
likelihood_reason: Matches how many firms use AI today; it depends on training investment that is only partly in place.

title: Stalled Progress
author: World Economic Forum
desc: Steady AI progress meets persistent talent shortages. Gains are uneven and automation mainly fills gaps; AI-proficient firms pull ahead, routine roles are cut and inequality widens.
likelihood_reason: Uneven gains, skills shortages and leading firms pulling ahead describe current conditions.

title: AI 2040: Plan A
author: Larsen, Dean, Halstead, Lifland, Greenblatt & Kokotajlo (AI Futures Project)
desc: After AI automates white-collar work in 2027–28, an international deal with full transparency over AI R&D slows the race: controlled scaling to expert level by 2035, a deliberate pause, then supervised progress to superintelligence by 2040, avoiding an unprecedented concentration of power.
likelihood_reason: Needs both very fast capability gains and a verified US–China deal with total R&D transparency.
